title: Index the inbox: four hot queries, at most three indexes
problem: The messenger runs four hot queries (they're in the test file). Choose at most three CREATE INDEX statements so that every query is a SEARCH, the two ORDER BY queries need no sort step, the unread count and 'my chats' never touch the table, and no index is a prefix of another.
requirements: INDEXES contains only CREATE INDEX statements, at most three
MY_CHATS: a covering SEARCH on chat_members, no USE TEMP B-TREE
HISTORY_PAGE: a SEARCH using chat_id=? AND created_at<?, no USE TEMP B-TREE
UNREAD_COUNT: a SEARCH using a COVERING INDEX on chat_id=? AND created_at>?
SENT_IN_CHAT: a SEARCH using both chat_id and sender_id
No index's columns are a prefix of another index's columns
Don't change the queries or the schema
contract: inbox_indexes.INDEXES: list[str] of CREATE INDEX statements
expectedBehavior: Every query's EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows SEARCH with the listed columns, and the queries return the same rows as without indexes
edgeCases: The composite primary key (chat_id, user_id) can't serve a filter on user_id
A range (< or >) on an index column stops later columns from being searched
A covering index must contain every column the query reads
An index that is a prefix of another is redundant
hints: Conceptual: for each query, list the equality columns, then the one range or ORDER BY column, then the other columns it reads. Two of the four queries can share one index.
Specific: HISTORY_PAGE and UNREAD_COUNT both filter chat_id with = and created_at with a range. MY_CHATS reads only chat_id, so chat_id must be inside its index to make it covering.
Implementation: three indexes: chat_members (user_id, joined_at, chat_id); messages (chat_id, created_at); and messages on sender_id and chat_id. Check each with your explain() helper from L01.
evaluation: You can say for each index which query it serves and why its column order is what it is
